title: Marker.io vs Usersnap
kicker: · MARKER.IO VS USERSNAP · COMPARED FOR AGENCIES
headline: Marker.io vs Usersnap: which fits your agency?
standfirst: Marker.io turns an annotated screenshot into a ticket inside the tracker your developers already run. Usersnap turns a widget on your live product into a feedback, survey, and roadmap platform. The fork: one hands fixes to a dev team, the other hands insight to a product team.
disclosure: We make Superflow, a third option in this space. It appears once, at the end, clearly marked. Everything above it is a straight comparison.
dateline: Facts checked July 2026, from marker.io and usersnap.com.
shortAnswerPickLeft: if the fixes live in Jira, GitHub, or Linear and your developers want console logs, network requests, and session replay attached to every report.
shortAnswerPickRight: if you want a feedback platform that also runs surveys, a public feature-request portal, and a changelog alongside the reports themselves.
shortAnswerShared: Both assume a person finds every mistake.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Start with the question everything else depends on.
leftFacts: A person finds every issue, then reports it.
Its AI edits, translates, and titles report text; a Marker.io MCP feeds report context to outside AI agents for triage and fix suggestions. Nothing looks at the site to find issues.
rightFacts: A person, usually the end user, reports every issue through the widget.
Its AI sidekick categorizes, scores sentiment, summarizes, and drafts replies and hypotheses on feedback already submitted, both marked beta. It does not scan or test the live site.
dimensions.verdict: Even. In both tools, a person finds the mistake before either product ever looks at the site.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Both make sending feedback easy. Neither makes the yes formal.
leftFacts: Reporters submit free from the widget, no account, and can follow their own issues.
Ongoing client collaborators are paid Guest seats, 10 on Starter, 50 on Team.
A formal approval flow: not yet verified.
rightFacts: Anyone submits via the widget or a survey, no account or seat needed.
A public, limited board lets guests upvote and track tickets without a paid seat.
A formal approve or reject gate: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Sending feedback: even, both free and open. A recorded client sign-off: neither, pending verification.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: A picture of the page, or the page itself.
leftFacts: You annotate a captured screenshot of the page; the report carries the picture.
Widget on the live site, snippet or CMS plugin; browser extension for members on any webpage.
Session replay adds a video of the last three minutes, Team plan and up.
rightFacts: Feedback comes from a widget on your live site or app, or a browser extension, with on-page screenshot annotation; the team reviews in a shared dashboard.
Authenticated-site review as a named feature: not yet verified.
dimensions.rightVerified: verified usersnap.com/bug-reporting, July 2026 except where noted
dimensions.verdict: Even shape. Both put a widget or extension on the live page and annotate a screenshot there. Behind logins, both dash the same way.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal comments on every plan, including Starter.
rightFacts: Internal notes stay team-only in the dashboard; replies to the reporter go out by email.
dimensions.verdict: Even. Both keep the internal debate private and separate from what the reporter sees.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both attach context automatically. The depth differs by plan.
leftFacts: Screenshot plus environment details, browser, OS, webpage, screen size, on every plan.
Console logs, network requests, and session replay of the last three minutes, on the Team plan and up.
rightFacts: Manual annotated screenshots and screen recordings with voice, triggered when the reporter submits.
Auto metadata on every submission: URL, browser, device, OS, screen size.
Console and error log auto-capture: gated to Professional and up.
dimensions.verdict: Both gate their deepest technical capture behind a mid tier, Marker.io's Team plan and Usersnap's Professional plan. Even on structure. Marker.io names an automatic session-replay video; Usersnap's screen recordings start when the reporter triggers them.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Does project ten start smarter than project one?
leftFacts: No memory concept. Each project starts blank.
rightFacts: No memory concept. Nothing persists learned context across projects.
dimensions.verdict: Even: neither. Worth knowing before either accumulates years of client history.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: Both promise to sync back. The names on the list differ.
leftFacts: Feedback becomes a ticket in your tracker. Integrations: Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Linear, Azure DevOps, Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Monday.com, Notion, Basecamp, Shortcut, Teamwork, Wrike, plus Slack, Intercom, Zendesk, Sentry, FullStory, LogRocket.
Two-way Issue sync is a Team plan feature: Done in Jira flips the issue to Resolved in Marker.io. Azure DevOps plan gate: not yet verified.
rightFacts: Two-way sync with Jira, Jira Product Discovery, Azure DevOps, and Linear.
dimensions.verdict: Both sync two-way into Jira. Usersnap also names two-way sync for Jira Product Discovery, Azure DevOps, and Linear, and its 2,000-plus Zapier reach covers a longer tail; Marker.io's named list runs deepest on dev trackers.

dimensions.label: What it costs
dimensions.framing: The sticker and the caps are different numbers.
leftFacts: Starter $39/mo annual, $59 monthly: 3 users, 10 projects, 10 guests, 5k page views/mo.
Team $149/mo annual, $199 monthly: 15 users, 50 projects, 50 guests, 25k page views/mo.
Business: custom, yearly billing only. No Agency plan exists on marker.io/pricing. No free plan; 15-day trial, no card.
rightFacts: Free: first 20 feedback items, 5 seats, 500 feedback storage; deactivates after 90 days if not upgraded.
Starter $49/mo billed yearly, $59 monthly: 5 seats, 5 live projects, 500 feedback storage, 100k page views/mo.

Growth $109/mo yearly, $129 monthly: 10 seats, 15 live projects, unlimited storage, 500k page views/mo. Professional $189/mo yearly, $229 monthly, most popular: 20 seats, 20 live projects, 1M page views/mo. Premium from $369/mo yearly, from $449 monthly: 50 seats, 50 live projects, 2M page views/mo. Enterprise custom.
dimensions.verdict: Lowest entry sticker: Marker.io at $39. But Usersnap's $49 Starter allows 100k page views against Marker.io's 5k cap. Price the caps, not just the sticker.

thirdOptionBody: Both Marker.io and Usersnap assume a person finds every mistake. Superflow is a QA tool + a team: AI agents built from your checklist check every site change, your team decides, your client approves from a link.

faq.question: Which is better for a small agency?
faq.answer: Marker.io if your fixes live in a dev tracker and you want console logs and session replay attached. Usersnap if you want a broader platform: surveys, a feature-request portal, and a public guest board alongside the reports.

faq.question: Do clients need accounts?
faq.answer: No on both. Marker.io reporters submit without an account; Usersnap accepts feedback via widget or survey with no account or seat. Ongoing client collaborators are paid seats on Marker.io.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Marker.io's Starter is $39/mo annual but caps at 5k page views. Usersnap's Starter is $49/mo annual with 100k page views. Price the cap that matches your traffic, not just the sticker.

faq.question: Can either check the site itself?
faq.answer: No. Both collect what a person already found. Marker.io's AI edits report text; Usersnap's AI sorts and summarizes submitted feedback. Neither scans the live site. That's the third option above.

faq.question: Does either have a public board clients can use without logging in?
faq.answer: Usersnap does: a public, limited portal where guests upvote and track tickets with no paid seat. Marker.io's guest access becomes a paid seat once a reporter needs to follow more than their own issue.
